candidates.change_summary: Replace the addition into userBalance with a subtraction, so calling addToBalance decreases the stored balance for the msg.sender.
Replace the update to only set the balance to msg.value (overwrite rather than add), so addToBalance sets the caller's balance to the sent value.
Change the reentrancy guard to set locked_ = false before executing the function body, allowing entry while locked and altering observable effects.
Remove the require check so the guard no longer prevents reentrancy, enabling possible reentrant differences in balances.
Replaced the return expression to return double the stored balance, changing observable return values.
Replaced the return expression to return zero for every address, changing observable return values.
Replaced the return expression to return the caller's balance instead of the supplied address, changing observable return values when caller differs from argument.

Replace the addition of msg.value into userBalance with setting userBalance[msg.sender] = msg.value (overwrites instead of increments). This changes the post-call balance observable after addToBalance.
Remove the reentrancy guard by making the modifier a no-op (drops locking behavior), which can change observed balances after addToBalance if reentrancy occurs.
Move setting userBalance[msg.sender] = 0 before the external call so the balance is cleared before the call.
Remove the line that sets userBalance[msg.sender] = 0 so balance remains after withdraw (no zeroing).
Remove reentrancy guard's locking so the modifier no longer prevents reentrancy (delete setting locked_ = true and reset), enabling reentrant calls to affect balances during withdraw.
Move zeroing of userBalance to before the external call so balance is set to 0 prior to the external call.
Remove the line that zeroes the user's balance after the external call, leaving the balance unchanged after withdrawBalance.
Remove the locking behavior by deleting the setting of locked_ to true, making the modifier not prevent reentrancy.
